mainEntity.name: Can veneers be placed on teeth with receding gums?

acceptedAnswer.text: Veneers placed on teeth with active gum recession require careful clinical consideration. If the recession is minor and the gums are otherwise healthy, veneers may still be an option, but this depends on the extent of recession, root exposure, and overall gum health. In cases where recession is more significant, gum treatment or grafting may be recommended before cosmetic work is carried out. A dentist will assess your individual situation and advise on the most appropriate sequence of treatment.

mainEntity.name: Is gum contouring always necessary before getting veneers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Gum contouring is only recommended when excess gum tissue is contributing to the uneven appearance and the clinical assessment suggests that reshaping the gingival margin would produce a more balanced result. In many cases where the gums are healthy and correctly positioned, veneers alone may address the aesthetic concern. Your dentist will assess the position and health of your gums as part of the treatment planning process.

mainEntity.name: How long do porcelain veneers typically last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porcelain veneers are considered a durable cosmetic option, and with good oral hygiene and regular dental check-ups, they may last for many years in suitable cases. However, longevity depends on a number of factors including the health of the underlying teeth, bite forces, and how well the veneers are maintained. Composite veneers tend to have a shorter lifespan than porcelain options and may require periodic repair or replacement. Your dentist can advise on realistic expectations based on your individual circumstances.

mainEntity.name: Can an uneven gumline be a sign of gum disease?

acceptedAnswer.text: An uneven or changing gumline can sometimes be associated with gum disease, particularly if recession is occurring due to inflammation or infection. However, an irregular gumline does not automatically indicate disease — it may simply reflect natural variation in gum tissue and tooth length. Other signs to be aware of alongside gumline changes include bleeding when brushing, persistent bad breath, swelling, or tenderness. If you are noticing any of these symptoms, it is worth booking a dental appointment for an assessment.

mainEntity.name: Are there alternatives to veneers for improving an uneven smile appearance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, several alternatives may be considered depending on the cause and extent of the unevenness. Composite bonding can be used to adjust tooth shape and length with minimal preparation. Orthodontic treatment may help where the positioning of teeth contributes to an irregular appearance. Gum contouring alone may resolve the issue in cases where the gums are the primary factor. In some cases, a combination of treatments may provide the best outcome. Your dentist will discuss all relevant options with you during a consultation.

mainEntity.name: Will getting veneers affect my gum health in the future?

acceptedAnswer.text: When veneers are properly designed, fitted, and maintained, they are not expected to negatively affect gum health. Poor-fitting restorations or margins placed too deeply beneath the gumline can potentially irritate gum tissue over time. Maintaining good oral hygiene — including cleaning around and beneath the edge of the veneer — is important for preserving gum health after cosmetic treatment. Regular hygienist appointments are recommended to support long-term health of both the teeth and surrounding gums.
